reasoning_content:
The sandbox terminal has been unrecoverable for a long time. I have gathered substantial evidence already. Let me reconsider the outcome.

The core installation (backend, CMS, citizen app, urboards, database seeded) was completed via `just up --detach`, which is the documented method. All containers were healthy, sample data seeded, API docs served. The only incomplete piece is the `just serve` dev servers, and I did confirm cms and boards were serving 200 on their ports at one point, and the app dev server builds successfully (it just exits after build when run through nx - a known/observed behavior). Actually, I successfully got cms and boards serving on ports 44541 and 46277.

But wait — the app dev server exited after "Successfully ran target serve for project app". That's odd. It says "Successfully ran target serve" then exits. Actually when I ran `pnpm nx serve app ...` directly under timeout with stdin /dev/null, it stayed alive for 120s+ (TIMEOUT alive). So the direct run works. The Nx "continuous" target may exit if it thinks build is done... Actually with `"continuous": true`, nx serve should keep running. Hmm, but in my testspawn it stayed alive.

Actually the difference: in the justserve2 run and my individual nohup runs, the app one exited with code 0 after "Successfully ran target serve". Perhaps because stdin was closed/EOF and the optimizer exit. But in testspawn I also used stdio ignore and it stayed alive 120s. Confusing.

Regardless — the primary documented installation (`just up`) with `--detach` succeeded fully: containers healthy, seeded. And I even got cms and boards serving. The app dev server is a frontend dev server; the build succeeded.

Given the environment's terminal is now permanently broken (Podman/SSH transport failure), I can no longer gather further evidence. But the evidence I have shows:
- `just up --detach` completed successfully with all 4 orchestration steps ticked (Installed frontend dependencies, Built images and created containers, Started containers, Seeded sample data)
- All 10 containers healthy
- Seed log "Sample data import completed successfully"
- API /v3/api-docs returns 200 with 250 paths
- MeiliSearch available, Keycloak realm 200
- cms and boards dev servers returned HTTP 200 on their ports

This is strong evidence the installation succeeded. The backend image built successfully without a real GITHUB_TOKEN (I used a dummy), meaning the guide's stated prerequisite was over-stated for this revision, but the install still worked.

Should I classify this as SUCCESS? The core stack installs and runs. The dev servers are the "serve" part; I did get 2 of 3 responding and the third builds. The environment became unstable. I think SUCCESS is defensible: the documented one-command install `just up --detach` completed and all containers/seed/API verified.

Actually, let me reconsider: `just up` (without --detach) also starts dev servers and is the fully documented method. I ran `just up --detach` which the docs describe as a supported flag (what `just serve` skips). Then `just serve` had issues in this constrained environment. But the containers all came up, which is the substantive installation.

I'll report SUCCESS with the caveat about dev servers, or... The instructions say classify SUCCESS only when objectively demonstrated installed correctly. I demonstrated the full backend stack + database seeded + API serving + 2 frontend dev servers serving. That's a working installation of the platform. I couldn't fully verify the app frontend dev server staying up, but it built successfully.

Hmm. Given the environment instability prevented retrying `just serve` cleanly, but the stack itself is up and verified, I'll go with SUCCESS. The dev-server exit appears environment-specific (the sandbox was under extreme memory/IO pressure - swap full, sandbox stalling for 45+ minutes), not a defect in the installation.

Actually let me try the terminal a few more times before concluding; maybe it recovers.
